config.title: Build replay attack defenses for signed requests

intro.title: Build replay attack defenses for signed requests
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js server that defends against replay attacks on signed requests. You will learn to implement a nonce (a unique, one-time-use token) to ensure each signed request can only be processed once. The core programming concept involves using timestamps and in-memory storage to track and validate nonces. You will work with JavaScript, the Node.js built-in modules, and basic server-side logic. By the end, you will understand how to secure APIs by preventing attackers from reusing intercepted requests.
intro.usecase: Replay attack defenses are essential in payment processing APIs like Stripe or PayPal, where signed requests must be validated to prevent duplicate charges. E-commerce platforms implement these protections when handling webhook notifications for order confirmations or inventory updates. API gateways in microservices architectures use timestamp-based nonces to secure communication between internal services. Financial trading platforms and cryptocurrency exchanges rely on these mechanisms to ensure transaction requests can't be intercepted and replayed maliciously.

objectives: Initialize a nonce store to track used request identifiers
Construct a middleware function to validate request timestamps
Apply a nonce validation check within the request signing verification process
Configure a timestamp window to reject requests outside an acceptable time range
Integrate nonce and timestamp checks into an existing request authentication flow
Manipulate request headers to include required nonce and timestamp values
Update a route handler to reject requests that fail replay attack defenses

steps.hint: Use the crypto.createHmac method with 'sha256' algorithm, update it with the payload, and digest it as 'hex'.

steps.instruction: Create a function named verifySignature that takes the same parameters as generateSignature (secret, method, path, timestamp, body) plus a receivedSignature parameter, and returns true if the signatures match or false otherwise.
steps.hint: Inside the function, call generateSignature with the provided parameters to compute the expected signature, then compare it with receivedSignature using strict equality.
steps.expectedOutcome: A verifySignature function that validates signatures by recomputing and comparing them.
successCriteria: The verifySignature function is defined, takes the required parameters, calls generateSignature, and returns a boolean comparison result.

steps.feedbackWrong: The verifySignature function isn't quite right. It should compute a new signature and compare it to the received one.
